prompt:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{x+1}{x^{2}-x-6}$.

**(a)** Write down the equations of all asymptotes. **[2]**

**(b)** Find the intercepts with the axes. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $x^{2}-x-6=(x-3)(x+2)$: vertical asymptotes $x=3$ and $x=-2$ **(A1)**; the denominator has higher degree, so $y=0$ is the horizontal asymptote **(A1)**

**(b)** $x$-intercept $(-1,0)$ **(A1)**; $y$-intercept $\left(0,-\tfrac16\right)$ **(A1)**
